title: Attention in Psychology, Neuroscience, and Machine Learning
summary: A broad review of how attention is defined, measured, and implemented across psychology, neuroscience, and machine learning.
comparison: The best starting point for separating biological attention from the several operations called attention in artificial networks.
limit: A conceptual synthesis; it does not establish that transformer attention is a cortical mechanism.

title: The Normalization Model of Attention
summary: Models attention as modulation of stimulus drive within a divisive normalization framework, accounting for different forms of response gain.
comparison: A concrete biological computation to compare with artificial reweighting and competition.
limit: Divisive normalization and transformer softmax are different operations; any equivalence requires a specific derivation.

title: Shaping Functional Architecture by Oscillatory Alpha Activity: Gating by Inhibition
summary: Proposes that alpha-band activity suppresses task-irrelevant processing and shapes functional pathways.
comparison: Especially relevant to EEG: compares selection by suppressing irrelevant channels with selection by increasing relevant weights.
limit: Alpha gating is not a one-to-one implementation of a transformer mask or head.

title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Introduces the transformer, using multi-head attention and feedforward layers for sequence transduction.
comparison: Defines the artificial operation that most current brain–transformer comparisons try to explain.
limit: An engineering paper, not a neuroscientific account; biological comparisons in this catalogue are explicitly interpretive.

title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
summary: Derives a continuous-state modern Hopfield memory whose update corresponds to transformer attention and demonstrates useful memory layers.
comparison: Provides a precise mathematical bridge between attention and associative retrieval.
limit: Equivalence to an artificial associative-memory update does not demonstrate a biological synaptic implementation.

title: Relating transformers to models and neural representations of the hippocampal formation
summary: Shows that transformers with recurrent positional representations can reproduce spatially tuned representations and connect mathematically to hippocampal models.
comparison: Links attention-based retrieval to place/grid representations and hippocampal indexing.
limit: The result depends on architectural modifications and training; it is not a general claim about all transformers or biological attention.

title: Modeling attention and binding in the brain through bidirectional recurrent gating
summary: Combines bottom-up visual processing with top-down and lateral recurrent gating. The trained model reproduces several attentional behaviors and neuron-like response properties.
comparison: A direct architecture-level attempt to unify spatial selection, visual search, and binding through recurrent modulation.
limit: Qualitative similarities and architectural constraints support a model account; they do not identify the exact implementation in cortex.
